synopsis: Ground truth must independently describe the physical scene and machine state; using the production detector’s output as truth is circular and can conceal missed objects [f99, f5358, f5359]. Replay against this reference is an established way to baseline an existing warning system without driving the machine, but usable logs need synchronized raw sensors, machine signals, calibration and labels; valuable ignored-warning near misses often lack ground truth [f94, f520, f11899, f7943]. The recommended reference combines surveyed targets, reference lidar with RTK-GNSS/INS, and human-audited auto-labels, with complementary sensors and an explicit “truth unavailable” state when reference sensing degrades [f5197, f12715]. Ground truth itself requires calibration, synchronization and uncertainty budgets, with measurement uncertainty substantially below acceptance margins or measured discrepancies; otherwise reference errors can dominate system differences [f7473, f8222, f7474, f11243]. Weather facilities provide important validation references, but a 2019 survey says chambers cannot fully replace real weather, while a 2026 paper proposes rainfall corrections; reconstructed or generated environments likewise do not automatically supply trustworthy geometric truth [f5056, f5085, f5104, f4046]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, preparing a ground-truth specification alongside physical-test procedures, a soft-target kit and independent-test-body engagement is considered realistic by mid-2027, although labeling and ground truth are identified as likely replay bottlenecks [f851, f1144].

Both describe Pretoria’s surface GPS and underground lidar, camera and radar reference methodology.
The hybrid approach adds surveyed anchors and audited labels to the continuous reference.
Explains how detector-derived truth hides misses and falsely improves the baseline.
Specifies the recordings needed to make replay useful.
Sensor-model validation using fleet logs additionally requires permissible consent and data-rights status.
Both require calibrated reference measurements with timing and uncertainty treatment.
Reference inaccuracy can dominate differences and reverse apparent system quality.
Positioning accuracy constrains other metrics, explaining measurement uncertainty’s limiting role.

Qualifies facility-based weather truth with real-weather limitations and proposed rainfall corrections.

Nonmetric, uncertain geometry explains why generative world models remain least established for validation truth.
